value: What are the major components of any society's economy?
Which of the following is generally true of pastoralist societies in East Africa?
answers: Cattle functioned as their special purpose money in the past.
Women use their livestock to pay a bride price when they get married.
They have successfully resisted the use of general purpose money.
correct_answer: Cattle functioned as their special purpose money in the past.

value: Gift giving is a common form of non-market exchange within small-scale societies. Which of the following statements is true concerning this sort of exchange?
answers: The primary motivation for this form of economic exchange in small-scale societies is not economic but social.
It usually results in an inequality in the distribution of wealth within the community.
It is better to receive gifts from others because it results in your personal enrichment and increased political power.
correct_answer: The primary motivation for this form of economic exchange in small-scale societies is not economic but social.

value: The most common form of exchange in non-market economies between friendly small-scale societies is ____ .
answers: the sale of goods using general purpose money as a medium of exchange

value: According to this tutorial, the crucial difference between gifts and sales is that ____ .
answers: gifts create and strengthen social relationships while sales usually do not
sales are more efficient than gifts in exchanging goods and services
more kinds of things can be exchanged by selling
gifts are decorated with bow knot
correct_answer: gifts create and strengthen social relationships while sales usually do not

value: Which of the following things are usually considered to be important gifts in small-scale societies with non-market economies?
Which of the following statements is true of reciprocal gift exchanges in all societies?
answers: Participants in a gift exchange agree to receive a gift and repay it with another.
Reciprocal exchanges usually redistribute the wealth of a society in a way that causes some people to become richer than others.
Reciprocity requires that a gift be returned that has close to the same economic value.
correct_answer: Participants in a gift exchange agree to receive a gift and repay it with another.

value: Marshall Sahlins observed that there are three distinct types of reciprocity that occur in human societies around the world. Which of the following statements is a description of what he described as generalized reciprocity?
answers: gift giving without the expectation of an immediate return
an economic exchange in which there is an explicit expectation of immediate return.
an attempt to get someone to exchange something he or she may not want to give up or an attempt to get a more valued thing than you give in return
correct_answer: gift giving without the expectation of an immediate return

value: Which of the following would fit the definition of balanced reciprocity in North America today?
answers: exchanging Christmas gifts with your best friend at an office party
giving a birthday present to a member of your family
correct_answer: exchanging Christmas gifts with your best friend at an office party

value: Some economic exchanges are intended to distribute a society's wealth in a different way than exists at present. These are called ____ ?
Which of the following are examples of economic redistributive systems?
answers: rich people giving substantial amounts of money to charities
rich people paying a higher income tax rate than poor people
potlatch ceremonies of the Kawakiutl and some of their Indian neighbors

value: Men in indigenous societies of New Guinea wanting to increase their personal status and influence over others organized large ceremonies similar to the Kwakiutl potlatch. The most important things that were given away during these ceremonies in New Guinea were ______ ?
The relative social position of someone in a group or in society is referred to as a _______ .
The part our society expects us to play in a given status is referred to as a ____ ?

answers: are acquired by both birth and achievement
